messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-db-primary (pd: P12345) — high connection queue depth observed, 95th percentile wait > 2s across app-proxy-*.region-a :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: page sent to escalation policy 'eng-oncall' — primary oncall: sam (oncall)
sam (oncall): acked — looking
sam (oncall): quick check: dashboards show client_conn_queue spiking on primary-db-01 and 02, pgbouncer accept queue growing
maya (sre): seeing increased `pg_accept_queue` and `redis_timeout` in same timeframe; suspicious traffic pattern from mobile-api-region-a
jordan (db): under load, connections near max_connections on both masters; replicas healthy but lagging ~200ms
sam (oncall): can we temporarily raise pgbouncer pool and enable read-only fallback for non-critical routes?
jordan (db): we can bump `max_client_conn` on pgbouncer and move non-essential routes to read-only via feature-flag. Doing a small change:```
# increase pgbouncer max_client_conn
kubectl exec -it pgbouncer-01 -- psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_client_conn = 2000;" && kubectl rollout restart deployment/pgbouncer
```
sam (oncall): +1 plan. Maya, can you throttle the noisy upstream if possible? Tagging @mobile-api-team
maya (sre): pinged mobile-api-team in #product-api, they saw a deploy with higher concurrency. Asked them to rollback or reduce concurrency to 50% immediately.
pagerduty-bot: alert escalated to second-level after 5m (no stable ack)
lee (platform): suggested short-term mitigation: enable KV prefix caching for common auth tokens on edge to reduce DB hits — can be toggled via config: `edge.cache.auth_prefix=true`
ops-bot: automated runbook suggestion: "If DB conn queue > 1000, add pgbouncer instances (scale to +2) and set app-level retry-backoff to 200ms"
sam (oncall): scaling pgbouncer and adjusting app retry-backoff now. Running: `kubectl scale deploy pgbouncer --replicas=4`
jordan (db): scaled, verifying. Also applying a conservative PG parameter change to reduce idle timeout to free connections faster: `tcp_keepalives_idle=30` — rolling restart on 01 only to test impact
maya (sre): mobile-api reduced concurrency to 40% and toggled feature-flag for non-critical reports. Early signs: traffic to DB down ~35%
sam (oncall): metrics updating — accept queue dropped from 1800 -> 420 in 2m, 95th wait down to 400ms. Still seeing occasional 503s to a small subset of customers (region-a) — investigating customer impact
jordan (db): customers affected: ~0.6% of requests (mainly long-transactions hitting analytics queries). Suggest we route analytics to replica read pool for now
sam (oncall): routing analytics to replica pool via temporary routing rule. `--set route.analytics=read-replica` applied
ops-bot: automated check: replica lag within safe bounds (<500ms), routing change OK
maya (sre): confirm 503 count decreasing and latency restoring. Noticing one background job still causing spikes; paused by ops-bot: `job-scan-indexer` paused
pagerduty-bot: alert acknowledged by sam (oncall) at 6321456740
sam (oncall): handing off to lee, I'm out in 25m. Summary for handoff: initial spike due to higher upstream concurrency from mobile-api deploy; mitigations applied — pgbouncer scaled, app retry/backoff, read-only routing of non-critical routes, analytics rerouted to replicas, background job paused. Impact: transient 503s for ~0.6% customers (region-a) for ~12m window.
lee (platform): taking over. I'll monitor for 1h and coordinate post-incident RCA. Next steps: 1) confirm deploy rollback on mobile-api, 2) keep pgbouncer scaled for 15m, 3) schedule follow-up on slow analytics queries.
jordan (db): creating DB-side ticket to investigate long-running analytics queries and plan materialized view for heavy joins
maya (sre): updating incident channel with customer-facing blurb for support: "We've observed transient database capacity issues in region-a impacting a small fraction of requests; mitigations applied and service recovering. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."
sam (oncall): tagging @support to surface to any affected customers
support-bot: support tickets flagged: TKT-8891, TKT-8892 (customers reported elevated 503s)
lee (platform): acked handoff. If we see another spike, escalate to db-pager and rotate oncall. Otherwise I'll set the incident to monitoring and create a postmortem owner.
incident-bot: incident moved to 'monitoring' at 6321456830 — no active pagers pending.
sam (oncall): thanks all — great fast triage. Postmortem: sam+lee+jordan+maya assigned
